entity_ranked_evidence.title: Specific Performance Decree Survives Delay: Supreme Court Rejects ‘Hyper-Technical’ View | Specific Performance Decree Survives Delay: Supreme Court Rejects âHyper-Technicalâ View
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: The Supreme Court has clarified that courts have the power to extend the time fixed in a decree for performance of its conditions and that a slight delay, by itself, cannot defeat a decree for specific performance. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Manoj Misra allowed an appeal filed by Dr Amit Arya after finding that he had consistently shown readiness and willingness to perform his part of the agreement. The respondent objected to the execution on several grounds, including that the petition was filed 87 days after the two-month period mentioned in the decree, that no extension of time had been granted, and that the balance sale consideration had not been deposited at the time of filing the execution petition. The bench directed that a copy of its judgment be sent to the executing court, which was asked to proceed in accordance with law and execute the decree of specific performance passed by the trial court.
